purpose: Independent review reproduction of the T42.H2b native sealed-input checks and of the kernel memfd sealing contract they depend on, executed off the T42.H1 selected host

reproduction_environment.vm: colima profile default, vmType vz, aarch64, 2 CPUs, 2 GiB
reproduction_environment.userspace_architecture: amd64 under Rosetta translation on an arm64 kernel
reproduction_environment.test_binary_built_by: GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -c ./spike/t421, on darwin/arm64 with go1.26.5
reproduction_environment.race_build_reason: the race detector requires cgo and a linux/amd64 C cross toolchain, which this host does not provide
reproduction_environment.go_toolchain_failure: cmd/go aborted with 'runtime: marked free object in span ... (bad use of unsafe.Pointer or having race conditions?)' at cmd/go/internal/modindex.getFileInfo while indexing the module cache; an emulation artifact, so only the pre-cross-compiled test binary was executed

emulation_artifact.symptom: a linux/amd64 binary occasionally exits 139 (SIGSEGV) before printing any output
emulation_artifact.control_experiment: a trivial hello-world linux/amd64 Go binary segfaulted 1 of 300 runs in the same container, and the t421 test binary invoked with -test.list, which runs no test at all, segfaulted 3 of 200
emulation_artifact.attribution: Rosetta translation process startup. Independent of phebs code, of the custody implementation and of every test assertion.
emulation_artifact.handling: exit 139 with no test output is discarded as environmental; only runs that reach test output are counted
emulation_artifact.warning_for_reruns: an emulated rerun will show occasional exit 139. It is not a custody failure and must not be recorded as one; rerun the affected repetition instead.

kernel_contract_probe.note: Standalone syscall probe, no phebs code, run on the same 6.8.0-117-generic kernel. Verifies the semantics input_custody_linux.go and its tests assume.
kernel_contract_probe.open_o_rdwr_on_write_sealed_memfd: succeeds once the mode is owner-writable
kernel_contract_probe.utimensat_on_fully_sealed_memfd: succeeds, moves Mtim, seal set stays intact at 0x2f, writes still EPERM

retained_probes.note: Both probes were originally scratch programs; they are now retained in the repository so every measurement above is re-derivable rather than trusted. Each is //go:build linux, uses golang.org/x/sys/unix instead of a hardcoded per-architecture syscall number, and builds on linux/amd64, arm64, 386 and arm. Neither exercises phebs code.

seal_probe.purpose: asserts the kernel memfd sealing contract input_custody_linux.go depends on, so a refusal inside ProtectLinuxExecutionInputs can be attributed to the host kernel rather than to the custody implementation

ctime_probe.purpose: measures the coarse inode timestamp behaviour that bounds metadata-drift detection, which is what made the original restored-chmod oracle unsound
ctime_probe.exit_zero_rationale: a low observability rate is the finding rather than a failure, so it exits zero unless it cannot run
ctime_probe.observed_run: 198/200 restore sequences left Ctim identical, ~1.000104 ms effective granularity, 200/200 unrestored drift detected, explicit utimensat drift observable with the seal set intact at 0x2f, exit 0

flake_diagnosis.status: pre-existing at the reviewed head; not introduced by any correction
flake_diagnosis.failing_assertion: input_custody_linux_test.go:150 'allowed non-execute metadata drift must still invalidate custody'
flake_diagnosis.failing_variant: executable=false (21-byte fixture); executable=true passed, doing more work before the drift
flake_diagnosis.mechanism: the test chmod'ed a sealed memfd to add owner-write and restored the original mode, then required Check to refuse through Ctim; Linux stamps inodes from a coarse clock, so a restore inside one tick changes no compared field and Check correctly accepts
flake_diagnosis.probe_restore_sequences_leaving_ctim_ide: 198 of 200 with the retained t42h2b-ctime-probe, and 199 of 200 with the scratch probe that first diagnosed it; the rate varies per run, which is the finding rather than a fixed figure
flake_diagnosis.probe_effective_inode_timestamp_granular: ~1.000104 ms, measured as 40 distinct Ctim values in 40.004193 ms of continuous chmod
flake_diagnosis.security_impact: none. The seals deny writes independently of mode, so a same-tick restored chmod gains nothing; metadata comparison is defense in depth, not the load-bearing control.
flake_diagnosis.documentation_impact: the PLAN ADR and operations guide claimed detection of any non-execute permission drift; both now state the same-tick boundary explicitly
flake_diagnosis.recorded_host_explanation: the T42.H1 host passed 20 race repetitions by timing margin, not by guarantee

corrected_reproduction.rebase_note: the corrections were originally authored on 56970e99, stacked on the reviewed head 8f1a4fc7. While the review was in progress, PR #58 merged T42.H2c into the H2b branch, advancing it to bbcad9cf, and PR #57 merged that branch into H2a. The corrections were therefore rebased onto bbcad9cf. Both corrected source files are byte-identical before and after the rebase, because H2c touches neither; only the surrounding tree, the commit identifiers and the test-binary digest changed. The superseded pre-rebase identifiers were 56970e99 (corrections), 23c9905a (binding), 74554873 (probes) and d4c59234 (attribution).
